defects.summary: The V0.D5 fix (7fec27e) hoisted the degraded federated report out of the `current_exit -eq 0` branch, so on a federated lock whose PRIMARY question could not be answered the run now blames the federated half for a primary-side failure — and swallows the accurate message that used to be printed.
defects.evidence: scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1191. Measured on a fixture I built: a federated lock pinning an unresolvable primary ref (9999...), run three ways against the same fleet harness. (a) branch tip, both scoped flags present: `ERROR: bumporg/repo-badprim: could not decide whether skills.lock is current — ERROR: cannot resolve ref '9999...' in <registry>` — accurate. (b) branch tip, both flags stripped: `ERROR: bumporg/repo-badprim: could not read this lock's federated half — ERROR: cannot resolve ref '9999...' in <registry>` — the unresolvable ref is the PRIMARY's, in the PRIMARY's checkout, and the lock's federated half is intact. (c) pre-fix script at 4c505e3, same stripped generator: `could not decide whether skills.lock is current` — accurate. So the degraded path is the only one that misattributes, and it did not before this commit. The new block also spends a full combined `--check-current` on a lock already known unanswerable and then `continue`s, so the primary-side report at line 1306 is never reached.

defects.summary: `self_named_note` is unconditional on $FED_ADVANCE_AVAILABLE — the same shape as the BLOCKING defect — so on a degraded run a self-federating lock's PR body asserts `--check-current --only` and `--repin-source` behaviour from a generator that has neither flag.
defects.evidence: scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1938-1945 (and the matching log() at :1125). Measured: self-federating lock (bumporg/agentskills as both primary and a source), both flags stripped. Body says: "A `--check-current --only bumporg/agentskills` has two answers under that one name, so the question was not put; `--repin-source` refuses that name outright for the same reason." Neither flag exists on that generator — the run had already emitted `::warning::... has no '--check-current --only <REGISTRY>'` and `... has no '--repin --repin-source <REGISTRY>@'` — so the stated reason no question was put is false, and the flag whose refusal is described was never available. The three-state fix in 72c994e covered the per-source LIST but not this paragraph beside it. Same log line fires in degraded mode with the same wrong reason.

defects.summary: A hollow assertion introduced by the V1.D4 fix: the needle it forbids has never existed in the file it greps, in either version, so the guard is a green light wired to nothing — the exact defect class 1c49d62/c7e5569 were written to close.
defects.evidence: test/run-tests.sh:5760-5763 — `assert_not_contains "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh" "can never separate a headline from the command" "slice: no comment promises a guarantee this slice does not have"`. Counted directly: `git show 4c505e3:scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh | grep -cF 'can never separate a headline from the command'` = 0, and the same grep on the current file = 0. The only occurrence of anything near that phrase anywhere in the repo is test/run-tests.sh:1067, inside the stub generator's own heredoc, and it reads "must never separate a headline from the command that fixes it" — which the needle would not match either. So unlike the other three needles this round repaired (each 1 -> 0 across the fix), this one is 0 -> 0 and cannot go red for any edit that reintroduces the absolute in the wording the script would actually use.

defects.summary: On the federated-only path (repin_reason=federated) the PR body now contradicts itself: the header says a federated source moved "and nothing else", and the hoisted evidence block three paragraphs later says a federated source moved "too".
defects.evidence: scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1737 vs :1798. Captured body for bumporg/repo-fed-current in a normal fleet run: header "**What moved:** a FEDERATED source, and nothing else.", why_note "What has moved is a federated source, whose bundles this lock also installs and whose pin only `--repin-source` advances.", then immediately "**A FEDERATED source moved too, and its pin advances with this PR.** Its bundles are installed by this lock and only `--repin-source` advances its pin." — "too" asserts something else also moved, which the header denies, and the second sentence restates the first almost verbatim. Pre-fix this block lived inside the `federated` branch with no such heading (`git show 4c505e3:scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh` has zero matches for "moved too"); 7732439 hoisted it and gave it wording written for the primary-also-moved case.

defects.summary: `derived_note`'s new sources-aware branch sends the reader to "the ref listed for it below" on a path where nothing is listed below — a self-federating lock, whose second entry's digests really are derived at a ref the body never names.
defects.evidence: scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1843-1848 keys on `${#source_registries[@]} -gt 0`, but `federated_lines` is built by a loop that skips `$reg == $primary_registry` (:1918), so a lock whose only source IS its primary produces an empty list and federated_note becomes "**No federated source in this lock could be asked about.**". Captured body for bumporg/repo-selffed: "...`bumporg/agentskills`'s own bundles at `8b159af`, and each federated source's at the ref listed for it below, in the repository that publishes it." followed by no list at all. The self-named entry's pin is carried through at the OLD ref (a988f05, asserted by the suite itself) and its digests are re-derived there, so in the general case — a self-named entry carrying real bundles rather than this fixture's empty one — the body promises a pin it never prints. Same dangling sentence appears on the degraded self-federating run.

defects.summary: The format+federated repro_note claims "The whole of it was <command>" for a command that omits --repo, --source-repo and -o, so it is not the whole invocation and will not run — a weaker claim than the unbranched sentence it replaced, which quoted a line that did carry those placeholders.
defects.evidence: scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1687-1690, built from `repin_command_shown` (:1459-1463). Captured bumporg/repo-fmtfed body: "The whole of it was `python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --ref f867ec9... --repin-source 'bumporg/cms-platform@'`". The actual invocation (:1470-1476) also passes `--repo "$primary_dir"`, `--source-repo bumporg/cms-platform=<path>` and `-o skills.lock`; --source-repo is not optional for a federated re-pin (the generator exits `ERROR: <reg>: no checkout — pass --source-repo`). The quoted --check-format remediation line directly above it, by contrast, does carry `--repo <a clone of the registry this lock names> -o <this lock>`, so a reader comparing the "half" with the "whole" sees the whole missing pieces the half had. The comment at :1455-1458 justifies dropping runner paths; the body's word "whole" is what the comment does not license.

defects.summary: The stub inventory added for V2.D7 states a count that its own list contradicts three lines later.
defects.evidence: test/run-tests.sh:5465-5466: "THE STUB INVENTORY, recorded so the next flag does not rediscover it. There are FOUR generator stand-ins in this file, and only the first is under test here:" — followed by a FIVE-item list (write_stub_generator, generator-no-repin.py, generator-no-check-format.py, generator-format-error.py, generator-errline.py) and then "The last four carry neither...", which is only coherent for five. The fix report itself says the inventory "names all five stand-ins now present". The file in fact holds more surgery-derived stand-ins than either number covers: generator-no-scoped-flags.py, generator-degraded-fed.py, generator-only-bundles.py and generator-missing-{only,repin-source}.py. A comment that asserts a checkable count and gets it wrong is the thing this repo's own rule forbids.
